preamble: No verified case of a direct /s/ > /d͡ʒ/ sound change has been found. The previously cited Hruso example ('three' from Proto-Tibeto-Burman *sum) is not supported: comparative work on the Hrusish languages reconstructs Proto-Hrusish *gə-θəm 'three' and describes PTB *s- as shifting to a dental stop or fricative, not to a postalveolar affricate. Routes from /s/ to /d͡ʒ/ normally pass through /ʃ/, /z/ or /ʒ/ and belong to those intermediate cells.

examples.note: Shows PTB *s- > dental *θ in Hrusish, not /d͡ʒ/; the earlier claimed Hruso form /d͡ʒə/ could not be verified

sources: Bodt, T. A., & Lieberherr, I. (2015). First notes on the phonology and classification of the Bangru language of India. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area, 38(1), 66–123. https://doi.org/10.1075/ltba.38.1.03bod
